ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of every UBO, general partner, authorised representative and day-to-day manager against: the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit's PEP classifications, CSSF and public national freezing lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, EU terrorist list, and applicable French/German/Belgian ancillary EU listings; adverse media screening and politically exposed person checks are required before any funds are accepted or any filing is made to the RCS or RBE.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal, lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script. Names may be in a foreign language but must be readably transliterated into Latin characters; if the true corporate name is in a non-Latin script, a Latin-script transliteration must be deposited with the RCS. The name must be lawful, non-confusing, not misleading, and must comply with public policy; for an SCSp the registered name should include the element 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' where the commercial name does not otherwise make the legal form evident.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the RCS within 15 days accompanied by a reasoned rebuttal. A further appeal may be brought before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within a three-month period under Luxembourg administrative procedural rules. A name reservation is not automatically renewable; the applicant must re-file after expiry or apply for a new reservation before converting it to a definitive registered name at incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or PO-box address is not acceptable for an SCSp. A Luxembourg-registered domiciliation provider may act as registered office holder only with a physical street address in Luxembourg, a signed domiciliation agreement, and a professionalized local compliance function. The SCSp must additionally evidence substance appropriate to its franchise licensing and royalties-supply-chain activities, including local bank account, local management, board/partner decisions made in Luxembourg, and adequate reporting and administrative records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% risk of unannounced physical inspection during the first three years; the likelihood materially increases if the SCSp is mass-domiciled at a shared address without independent local substance or if it records royalty revenue without corresponding locally controlled operational functions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; coordinated through the Luxembourg single e-government portal MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for foreign entities: (i) Apply for an RCS registration via MyGuichet.lu using the coordinated e-registration form; the RCS issues a national business number (matricule) that constitutes the statutory Luxembourg tax identification number (TIN) for the SCSp. (ii) For VAT, file a VAT registration declaration (formulaire 106/DC) with the AEDT, either on paper or via MyGuichet.lu, at least 15 calendar days before commencing taxable supplies. Non-established foreign entities are required to register directly with the AEDT regardless of turnover level (no threshold); a Luxembourg VAT identification number with the format 'LU' followed by 8 digits is issued together with a certificate of taxable status (attestation d'assujettissement). (iii) Foreign partners of a fiscally transparent SCSp without a permanent establishment in Luxembourg do not require a Luxembourg TIN for income tax purposes if their Luxembourg-source income is limited, but must supply their home-jurisdiction TINs to the SCSp for exchange-of-information and ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is a partnership without legal personality and is by default fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax; profits, gains and losses flow through to its partners in proportion to their capital interests and are taxable only at partner level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Opaqueness election (corporate check-the-box-style): Under Article 5 of the Law of 23 December 2016, an SCSp may irrevocably elect to be treated as a corporate taxpayer subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax if (i) 100% of its partnership interests are held by Luxembourg corporate taxpayers that are fully subject to corporate income tax and net wealth tax, or (ii) its partnership interests are listed on a regulated exchange. The election is binding and applies from the start of the fiscal year. Hybrid mismatch elections and adjustments are governed by the ATAD 2 implementation (Law of 20 December 2019), under which the Luxembourg tax administration may re-characterize the SCSp's transparency or an investor's tax treatment where structured arrangements create double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes with a non-EU jurisdiction, and in such cases the taxpayer may elect the appropriate offsetting/mirror adjustment mechanism subject to advance tax-ruling confirmation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) per the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, harmonized with the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small businesses eligible for the small-business exemption; EUR 10,000 annual EU distance-selling and electronically-supplied-services threshold for EU-established suppliers; NO registration threshold for non-established (foreign) taxable persons - any taxable supply made in Luxembourg (including intra-Community acquisitions, imports, and deemed supplies of goods or services) triggers mandatory VAT registration unless reverse charge, import VAT deferral, or OSS/IOSS schemes apply. For the SCSp franchise business, registration is therefore driven by the existence of a Luxembourg taxable supply (e.g., domestic syrup sales to Luxembourg franchisees), not by a turnover ceiling.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose a mandatory B2B electronic-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance regime. E-invoicing is accepted in structured formats (Factur-X/UBL, PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0, EDI) and must evidence authenticity of origin and integrity of content; paper invoices remain lawful. B2G invoicing to Luxembourg public authorities is mandatory in the European standard EN 16931 structured format through the PEPPOL network. No digital stamping, tax-authority clearance API, or invoice pre-validation is required for VAT purposes; however, recapitulative statements (Intrastat/EC sales listings), transaction-level reporting for e-commerce (OSS/IOSS), and the obligation to retain invoices and export evidence for at least 10 years apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported by the SCSp or on its behalf from the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg to a non-EU destination qualify for the 0% export exemption under Article 42(1) of the Luxembourg VAT Law, provided the exporter holds contemporaneous documentary proof of removal from the EU within the required timeframe and the goods are dispatched/transported outside the EU. Franchise and royalty services (boba-tea brand licence, know-how, supply-chain advisory) sold by the SCSp to non-resident franchisees are business-to-business services; under the general B2B place-of-supply rule they are taxable in the customer's jurisdiction (reverse charge) and therefore fall outside Luxembourg VAT - no Luxembourg VAT is chargeable and no refund claim arises on those fees. Exported syrups, toppings, packaging materials and equipment sold to non-EU franchisees qualify for the zero rate; exports to EU franchisees are intra-Community supplies, zero-rated only with a valid EU customer VAT number and a correct EC sales listing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document / ATLAS AES export declaration) with customs office of export and exit confirmation
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing dispatch from the EU to a destination outside the EU
CMR road consignment note or other export transport document establishing removal from the EU territory
Commercial invoice referencing the export declaration, including HS codes, quantities, unit values and Incoterms
Proof of payment / bank transfer instruction or foreign inward remittance certificate confirming receipt of export proceeds
Franchise contract, delivery notes, and warehouse/picking records evidencing the commercial substance of the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may revisit export zero-rating in post-clearance audits; where the required export documentation is absent, incomplete or contradictory, the 0% exemption is clawed back and VAT becomes payable at 17% together with default interest of 0.8% per month (increased to 1% per month in cases of fraud or deliberate intent) from the date the tax would have fallen due. Unjustified or repeated zero-rating claims expose the SCSp to a 50% fraud surcharge (majoration d'impôt) on the evaded VAT, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), with penalties up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment ranging from 8 days to 5 years. Additional consequences include disqualification of the responsible manager, revocation or suspension of the statutory franchise/business licence, inclusion in the AEDT's public control list, and, for hybrid or conduit arrangements, recharacterization under ATAD 2 resulting in further disallowed deductions and joint liability of partners.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in conjunction with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the BCL administers balance-of-payments statistics and payment system liquidity, while the CSSF supervises domestic credit institutions, AML/CFT conduct, and the registration of financial sector participants.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible within the eurozone; Luxembourg imposes no exchange control restrictions on current or capital account transactions under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Part XI of the Luxembourg General Law on money and finance. Capital contributions, dividend and profit distributions, royalty payments, and liquidation proceeds may be remitted freely to any jurisdiction, subject only to EU/UN sanctions screening, AML/CFT verification, and the obligation of resident entities to report cross-border flows to the BCL for statistical purposes. The key practical hurdle is not currency convertibility but the transparent tax classification of the SCSp, which is a partnership without separate legal personality; profit attribution follows the partnership agreement, and no Luxembourg withholding tax applies on distributions to non-resident partners provided the partnership is not fiscally opaque and the partners are not Luxembourg residents engaged in a taxable permanent establishment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Luxembourg or in the eurosystem legal framework. Export receipts in foreign currency (e.g., USD, CNY, TWD) may be retained in foreign currency accounts, converted to EUR at freely negotiated market rates, or used directly for settlement of trade payables, provided that the underlying transactions are economically substantiated and properly documented for BCL balance-of-payments reporting and CSSF AML supervision.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (SCSp held in the name of the general partner for the account of the partnership)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with material legal constraints. A Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institution (EMI) or payment institution (PI) authorised by the CSSF is acceptable for non-core collection of franchise royalty inflows, but the SCSp, having no separate legal personality, must open the account through its general partner; fund safeguarding rules require the EMI to hold client funds in segregated accounts, which can accommodate the SCSp but adds an intermediation layer. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK or Baltic-licensed) are viable only under the PSD2 grandfathering and passporting rules; post-Brexit UK EMIs cannot passport into Luxembourg, and a non-EEA EMI would require an EU-authorised agent or principal model, which is operationally burdensome and raises second-tier AML scrutiny. Given the franchise's cross-border royalty flow and ISIC 5610 business scope, a tier-1 domestic bank remains the default treasury anchor; a Luxembourg EMI may be used solely as a low-liquidity, high-throughput collection arm.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory at initial onboarding: Luxembourg banks, following CSSF AML/CFT guidance and the Law of 12 November 2004, require the general partner's authorised signatories and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding more than 25% of the partnership interests to present original identification documents in person during the account-opening interview, unless a full reliance on KYC performed by another EU credit institution has been contractually established under Article 3-4 of that law. Remote opening is permitted only through qualified electronic identification/trust services under eIDAS (e.g., remote video identification with a death-of-person identity verification procedure approved by the bank's AML officer), but it is conditional on a low residual risk profile and, in practice, the initial account mandate of a newly formed SCSp is opened with at least one in-person meeting in Luxembourg; a notarised or apostilled power of attorney can replace the physical appearance of a non-resident limited partner but not that of the general partner's managing director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no separate legal personality — the bank may flag the absence of the entity from the Luxembourg trade register (RBE/RIB) and challenge the legal standing of the account applicant.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed and notarised partnership agreement (limited partnership agreement of the SCSp), the general partner's certificate of incorporation and current curriculum vitae, an excerpt from the Luxembourg Register of Commercial and Companies (RCS) evidencing the SCSp registration, the CSSF/MFSA-compliant beneficial ownership chain, and a written explanation from the authorised legal counsel confirming that the general partner acts for the joint account of the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex non-resident ownership chain with multiple limited partners located in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions, triggering enhanced due diligence under CSSF Regulation N° 12-02.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart with full percentage holdings and source-of-wealth declarations for each UBO above the 25% threshold; audited financial statements or opening balance sheet of the SCSp; commercial contracts evidencing the bona fide boba tea franchise business (franchise agreements, supply agreements, trademark licence); police certificates and international sanctions screening results for all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty and trade flows from unrelated franchisees may be screened as trade-based money laundering exposure (e.g., mismatches between royalty invoices and underlying cup volumes, syrups supply trades).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented transfer pricing policy aligned with the arm's-length principle, the standard franchise disclosure document, sample royalty invoices reconciled to franchisee point-of-sale reports, bills of lading and customs declarations for syrup shipments, and an independent AML risk assessment confirming the 'Low_Risk_Standard' classification of the ISIC 5610 commercial model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank may reject the SCSp because of the taxpayer classification and absence of a Luxembourg corporate tax certificate, fearing disguised distribution or financing arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Luxembourg tax opinion or advance tax confirmation stating the partnership's pass-through status, the absence of Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax within the SCSp, and the treatment of the franchise royalties as commercial income; a signed declaration of the general partner confirming no tax-driven structuring purpose; and the complete investor subscription agreements evidencing genuine capital commitments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols require all capital contributions to the SCSp to be wired via SWIFT MT103 using the bank's standard commercial wire fields, referencing the partnership name, the capital subscription clause of the partnership agreement, and the Luxembourg BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment equity, i.e., category 'S0501' (investment in equity capital) or the specific partnership capital code where locally approved by the bank; for loans from shareholders, the code 'S0503' (loans from parent and fellow subsidiaries) applies. Verification includes the submission of the board resolution or general partner resolution authorising the capital call, the capital call notice evidencing the amount and due date, and the signed subscription schedule; the receiving bank will perform a beneficiary identity match against the KYC file and may seek confirmation from the remitting bank (MT199) where the purpose code is inconsistent or where the remitter is not an established EEA financial institution or a pre-listed shareholder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed primarily through the euro payment system (TARGET2 and TIPS) for intra-EEA supplier payments, and via SWIFT MT103 for cross-border conventional wire transfers; for irrevocable trade commitments, a commercial documentary letter of credit governed by UCP 600 is issued by the bank (confirmation advised for Chinese and Taiwanese syrup suppliers), with remittance via MT202 COV when intermediary banks are required. Supplier payments out of the global treasury accounts must be supported by invoices, shipping documents, and, where applicable, the BCL BOP purpose code for goods and services; the treasury hub will additionally deploy ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002 messages for domestic direct debits and credit transfers, together with an intraday EUR cash-pooling overlay among the Luxembourg account, the franchise management company account, and local collection accounts to reduce funding gaps.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forwards (OTC) for conversion of North American royalty receipts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing offshore CNY (CNH) and TWD for Asian franchisee revenue streams, as the onshore renminbi and new Taiwan dollar are not freely deliverable
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/CNH, EUR/USD) for long-duration balance sheet hedging of supply chain obligations
FX options (plain vanilla calls and puts) for asymmetric protection of royalty streams while preserving upside
Commodity/interest hybrid swaps only where the underlying boba tea supply raw material price exposure is documented, though such instruments are disfavoured for ISIC 5610 standard operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (confirmation annuelle des beneficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial RBE filing each year; separate updated filing within 30 days of any transfer or change of beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative and criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 6 months for wilful failure by the general partner; entity flagged as non-compliant in the LBR portal and blocked from obtaining RCS extracts and certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual statutory accounts (depot des comptes annuels) in LBR eCDF format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end plus deposit within 1 month of approval; for a 31 December year-end the deposit must occur by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal demand by RCS registrar; court-ordered daily penalty payment ('astreinte') up to EUR 1,250 per day; criminal fine from EUR 250 to EUR 2,500; two consecutive years of default may trigger RCS strike-off ('radiation') and loss of access to certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business establishment authorization (autorisation d'etablissement) - maintenance and variation filings for boba-tea franchise licensing and beverage-syrup supply activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction generale de l'industrie (via the Guichet.lu e-desk)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Authorization is issued for an indefinite term and requires no annual renewal; within 30 days of any change in the licence holder, managing natural person, activity scope or premises, a variation or update filing is compulsory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid authorization after a material change is punishable by fines up to EUR 25,000 and an administrative suspension or closure order issued by the ministry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit by a Luxembourg 'reviseur d'entreprises agree' is mandatory only if the SCSp exceeds two of the three art. 34bis criteria under the Law of 19 December 2002 for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total above EUR 8.8 million, net turnover above EUR 17.6 million, or average workforce above 50 full-time equivalents; public-interest entities are always audited. A typical small IP-franchise SCSp remains below these thresholds and is exempt, though investors may require a voluntary audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002, based on the Plan comptable normalise; EU-endorsed IFRS is permitted voluntarily or for consolidation purposes; the RCS filing must be rendered in the LBR eCDF taxonomy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp is a separate RBE registrant: the general partner must file all beneficial owners (any natural person holding or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of partnership interests or control rights) and confirm the data annually within 30 days of the anniversary of the last filing; a nil-change confirmation is sufficient, but every transfer of partnership interests requires an updated filing within 30 days. Although the SCSp is tax-transparent, UBO filing remains a mandatory corporate secretarial obligation with criminal penalties for default.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (registre des associes) - records all limited partnership interests and transfers when the SCSp has elected legal personality
Minute book (registre des decisions) - records partner resolutions, management decisions and capital or royalty-related approvals
Statutory accounting books (grand livre, journal) - kept at the registered office together with supporting invoices and agreements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 15,000 per engagement for a voluntary certified audit of a small SCSp; statutory audit generally not required below the art. 34bis thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Aggregate statutory rate for fully taxable entities in Luxembourg City: 24.94% (corporate income tax 17% plus solidarity surcharge 7% of the CIT plus municipal business tax 6.75%). The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: the entity itself bears no CIT, and income is taxed at partner level; the 24.94% headline rate is relevant only if the SCSp validly elects opaque CIT treatment or where a partner is a Luxembourg-resident corporate entity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zero entity-level CIT for the transparent SCSp; election available for full CIT taxation (opaque treatment); 80% exemption for qualifying net IP royalty income under the Luxembourg IP box (subject to the 30% nexus ratio); 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction on qualifying increases in equity; none of these incentives remove the obligation to file returns and to maintain economic substance.
